title: Two Paid, Third Free
statement:
A shop runs a deal: every time you pay for two items, you may take one more item for free, as long as its price is no higher than the cheaper of the two you paid for. You may use the deal as many times as you like, and each item is bought once.

You get prices, the price of every item you want. Return the smallest total you have to pay to get all of them.

examples.why: Pay 9 and 7, take the 4 free, then pay 2. Paying 9 and 4 to get the 2 free would cost 20.
Two deals, each paying for two 5s and taking one free.
With only two items there is nothing to take for free.

hints: Which item should the most expensive two purchases unlock for free?
The free item can cost as much as the cheaper paid item. To save the most, make it as expensive as allowed.
Sort prices from high to low and walk in groups of three: pay for the first two of each group, skip the third.

explain.intuition:
The two most expensive items have to be paid for no matter what: nothing costs more than them, so neither can be the free one in a deal paid for by others. Once you pay for them, the best free item is the third most expensive, the highest price the deal allows. Then the same reasoning repeats on what is left.

So sort descending and skip every third item. Each skipped item is at most the cheaper of the two right before it, so every deal is legal, and the free items are as expensive as they can be.
steps: Add the price unless i % 3 === 2; those items are the free ones.
pitfalls: Sorting ascending and skipping every third from the start. With 4 items that frees the wrong one: the groups must be counted from the expensive end.
Taking the cheapest item free in every deal. The free item should be the most expensive one allowed.

solutions.title: Try every grouping
solutions.idea: Order the items every possible way and cut the order into threes; in each triple the cheapest is free. The best ordering is optimal.

solutions.title: Sort descending, skip every third
solutions.idea: Pay for the two most expensive remaining items and take the next one free, repeatedly.
